# 1 Enoch Chapter 11 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 11 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 11:1 — 'tilled' vs. 'farmed' for the agricultural activity

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall-be-tilled in-righteousness" | Preserves the specific agricultural term; 'tilled' implies plowing and preparation |
| LOGOS | "shall be tilled in righteousness" | Agrees with EMET |
| PNEUMA | "will be farmed in righteousness" | 'Farmed' is more broadly accessible but loses the specific tilling sense |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'tilled in righteousness' (EMET/LOGOS). 'Tilled' preserves both the specificity and the solemnity of the Ge'ez agricultural idiom. 'Farmed' (PNEUMA) is too generic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 11:2 — 'thousandfold' vs. 'ten-thousand' for the eschatological yield

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "each-measure [sown] shall-bear ten-thousand" | Preserves the Ge'ez large number literally |
| LOGOS | "each measure sown shall bear a thousandfold" | Normalizes to the standard eschatological idiom; cf. Amos 9:13 |
| PNEUMA | "every seed sown will yield ten thousand times over" | Dynamic; preserves the ten-thousand number |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS 'a thousandfold' as this reflects the standard textual tradition in most Ge'ez manuscripts (cf. Charles). The ten-thousand figure (EMET/PNEUMA) appears in some manuscripts but may be a scribal intensification. The general eschatological abundance is what matters, and 'thousandfold' connects the passage to the biblical tradition more clearly.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Textual note: manuscript variation exists on this number.

---

## Overall assessment

Chapter 11 is a brief, joyful two-verse passage with minimal divergence. Total significant divergences: 2 (both minor lexical/textual). The three translators agreed on the eschatological register and substance.
